name: San Ramón 15 iron-oxide mining
description: At San Ramón 15 near Taltal, northern Chile, hunter-gatherer-fisher groups mined an iron-oxide vein. Two excavated units preserve tailings, battered vein material and stone hammerstones. Separate dated levels document early extraction and renewed mining in the Late Archaic.

impact.note: One coastal community's early pigment mine shows organised extraction, a modest gain with no known later practice descending from it.

date.label: 10,494–10,146 cal BCE, unit 2 layer 5 shell
date.basis: Published calibrated bounds for shell sample Beta-280992 in unit 2 layer 5, with the article's local marine-reservoir correction.

events.statement: The central trench contains an early iron-oxide extraction deposit with rocks from the vein and stone mining tools.
events.caveats: The shell supplies a contextual date dependent on reservoir correction. The age of the first extraction and the dates of particular tools remain unresolved.

evidence.locator: pp. 466–470, Figs. 3 and 6 and Table 1, Beta-280992
evidence.supports: The dated early shell comes from unit 2 layer 5. Figures 3 and 6 show the extraction and deposit contexts, and the authors associate the date with early central-trench mining.

date.label: 8717–8472 cal BCE, dated charcoal in excavation unit 1
date.basis: Date of the stated witness or contextual sample, not a claim of global origin.

events.statement: At San Ramón 15 on the northern Chilean coast, excavation found iron-oxide workings and stone hammerstones associated with Early Holocene deposits.

evidence.supports: The authors describe iron-oxide workings and 491 hammerstones recovered from early Holocene levels. Unit 1 layer 7 charcoal sample UGAMS 5442 has a listed calibrated range of 8717–8472 BCE; it dates associated context rather than each tool or mine origin.

events.caveats: The displayed dates are a calibrated charcoal sample from unit 1 layer 7, not a direct date of the entire mine or of every hammerstone. Other material indicates earlier and later use; similarities with other mines do not establish transmission or a single origin.

evidence.supports: The authors describe iron-oxide workings and 491 hammerstones recovered from early Holocene levels. Unit 1 layer 7 charcoal sample UGAMS 5442 has a listed calibrated range of 8717–8472 BCE; it dates associated context rather than each tool or mine origin.

date.label: 2398–1954 cal BCE, unit 2 layer 3 charcoal
date.basis: Published calibrated bounds for charcoal sample UGAMS 5443 in unit 2 layer 3.

events.statement: Late Archaic miners returned to the trench after sediment had accumulated over early workings. Unit 2 preserves Late Archaic deposits above the earlier mining levels.
events.caveats: The charcoal dates an associated mining deposit. The date applies to this excavated layer within a separately documented phase of extraction.

evidence.locator: pp. 466–470, Figs. 3 and 6 and Table 1, UGAMS 5443
evidence.supports: Late and early archaeological levels in the central trench are separated by a natural colluvial deposit. Charcoal from the later level dates to 2398–1954 cal BCE.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated context interpreted as iron-oxide extraction in the excavators' report. The published adjusted marine-shell interval dates the deposit by association.

caveats: Dates are from associated shell or charcoal. The early shell calibration includes a local marine-reservoir correction. Natural sediment separates the early and late deposits in unit 2. The times of first use and final abandonment remain open.

research.note: The earlier review concerned the unit 1 layer 7 witness. The proposed additions use distinct unit 2 strata in the same excavation report.
